_comment: Every statement the 'In the Canon' notes (flavor.json novelNotes) and the ending texts make about Doyle's stories. status: 'secondary' = confirmed in at least one secondary source read on 2026-10-13 (see source); 'memory' = from the author's memory of the text, not yet checked against the story itself. The full texts (The Final Problem, 1893; The Empty House, 1903) are public domain; a human check against them is still to do for every 'memory' claim.

claims.statement: The Final Problem was published in the Strand Magazine in December 1893.
Holmes learns that most of Moriarty's gang have been arrested but that Moriarty has escaped and is pursuing him abroad.
Moriarty is never tried in the canon.
Watson is drawn away from the Falls by a letter claiming a dying Englishwoman at the hotel needs an English doctor.
Holmes tells Watson that his Baker Street rooms were set on fire the night before, an attempt to kill him and destroy his evidence.
Holmes meets Watson disguised as an aged Italian priest, sees Moriarty on the Victoria platform, and the pair leave the train at Canterbury as Moriarty's chartered one-coach special passes.
Watson returns to find a note, a cigarette-case and a stick, and footprints leading to the edge and not back; Holmes and Moriarty are presumed fallen.
claims.source: memory of the story; the note and decoy are confirmed secondarily in The Empty House summaries

claims.statement: The Reichenbach encounter is dated 4 May 1891 in the story.
In The Empty House Holmes says he was never in the abyss: he wrote the note with Moriarty's courteous leave and escaped.
Holmes then travelled in Tibet (as the Norwegian Sigerson), Persia, Mecca and Khartoum, and worked on coal-tar derivatives at Montpellier before returning.
claims.source: search summaries of The Empty House

claims.statement: Mycroft alone knew Holmes was alive and supplied him with money.
Holmes returned to London in 1894.
Colonel Sebastian Moran uses an air-gun in The Empty House and is caught by Holmes.
claims.source: search summaries of The Empty House

claims.statement: Moran is Moriarty's chief lieutenant and a celebrated heavy-game shot.
The Baker Street Irregulars are Holmes's street-boy agents, led by Wiggins, paid a shilling a day.
claims.source: memory of A Study in Scarlet and The Sign of Four

claims.statement: Mycroft is a government man of great reach in later stories.
In the story Moriarty visits Baker Street to warn Holmes off and Holmes refuses.
claims.source: memory of the story; the visit itself is confirmed secondarily

claims.statement: Watson records Holmes's long fits of languor and his use of cocaine in the earlier stories.
claims.source: memory of The Sign of Four and A Scandal in Bohemia

claims.statement: The crises, the closed hearing and second ledger, Larch, Pike, Alf, the Limehouse wharf and the alternate endings are the game's own invention and are labelled so.
In The Empty House Holmes returns in April 1894 over the Park Lane murder of Ronald Adair and reveals himself to Watson, who faints.
claims.source: search summaries of The Empty House; the faint and the disguise are from memory

claims.statement: Watson has suffered a bereavement (the death of his wife) in the years Holmes is away.
Holmes does work for the Government through Mycroft in later stories (for example The Bruce-Partington Plans), without any commission.
In Charles Augustus Milverton Holmes burns a blackmailer's letters rather than publish them.
The Whitehall road, the second ledger, Lord Harcastle, Superintendent Greaves, the case board and the examinations are the game's own invention.
The Strand (Hours, Hands, Wires) and its ruin ending are the game's own invention.

In A Scandal in Bohemia the King of Bohemia, masked and calling himself Count von Kramm, asks Holmes to recover a photograph of himself with Irene Adler before his betrothal to a Scandinavian princess; Adler leaves before Holmes can act, with a letter and her own photograph, and Holmes asks for the photograph in place of the King's ring.
claims.source: memory of the story (public domain); not yet checked against the text

claims.statement: Holmes pursuing Adler abroad, burgling her house, or telling the King nothing, and their consequences, are the game's own invention.

In The Adventure of the Speckled Band Dr Grimesby Roylott sends a swamp adder through a ventilator and down a dummy bell-rope to kill his stepdaughter, as he killed her twin; Holmes drives the snake back with a cane and Roylott dies of its bite.
claims.source: memory of the story (public domain); not yet checked against the text

claims.statement: A late strike, a warning to Roylott, a locked door and a Doctor who lives are the game's own invention.

In The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle Holmes traces a stolen jewel through a Christmas goose to James Ryder, and lets him go, saying it is the season of forgiveness and that he may be compounding a felony.
claims.source: memory of the story (public domain); not yet checked against the text

claims.statement: Sending for Lestrade, and Ryder's escape, are the game's own invention.

In The Adventure of the Red-Headed League a pawnbroker, Jabez Wilson, is paid four pounds a week to copy the Encyclopaedia Britannica so that his assistant, John Clay, can tunnel from the cellar to the vault of the City and Suburban Bank next door; Holmes, with Peter Jones of Scotland Yard and the bank director Mr Merryweather, waits in the vault and takes Clay with a hunting-crop, and his accomplice is taken at the shop. Holmes says it is an attempt to escape from the commonplace.
claims.source: memory of the story (public domain); not yet checked against the text

claims.statement: A successful robbery, and a quiet arrest that keeps the bank out of the papers, are the game's own invention.
